analysis.title: "Debt Market Limits Are Real And Binding": Top Goldman Trader Says Market Is Pricing 2027 As The AI Peak
key_insights: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky (head of EMEA one-delta trading) says the AI trade lacked support on Monday 11/2 even as energy fell about 8%. Gen AI fell 5%, AI healthcare 4%, optical 7.5%, neoclouds 6%. Homebuilders rose 4%, alternatives 3.5%, value 1.6%. High momentum lost 7% in one session.

Privorotsky decomposes the move into two parts: no support for the AI trade (an early bounce faded into the US session) and the energy collapse driving a bid to discretionary and retail. The result is a momentum unwind with shorts rising and longs falling.
SOX trades at about 12.16x blended 24-month forward earnings, near 2022 levels and below the Liberation Day and Iran escalation lows. Nvidia trades at 10x, its lowest multiple since 2013.

Privorotsky reads the multiples as the market pricing significant risk to estimates and possibly 2027 as a peak, because cost of capital and financing capacity limit how fast companies can build. He draws a parallel to late-90s tech, which built capacity before there was enough use for it.

Privorotsky says he is probably more in the bull camp (robotics has barely started, enterprise workflow automation has barely scaled) but states that corporate balance sheet capacity and debt market limits are real and binding.
SOX closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025, ending a 355-session streak above it (third longest in 10 years). It is 27.1% off its local high (Sharkey).

Overnight, Goldman's TSMC capex basket fell 8% and Korea AI fell 5%. Apple fell about 3% after hours on December-quarter gross margin guidance of 45-46%, hurt by higher memory costs. Privorotsky says AI demand supports memory pricing but competes for components and squeezes margins elsewhere.

Coppersmith says the AI debate is shifting from growth to the cost and financing of that growth. Hyperscaler capex is expected to reach $1.2 trillion in 2027, aggregate FCF turned negative in Q3, and upward earnings revisions are moderating, in crowded and heavily levered parts of the market.

Goldman research is more sanguine on financing: the funding gap may be smaller than feared, and GS Credit estimates about $500 billion of hyperscaler bond market capacity. Garrett relays that credit experts see AI financing needs that could surprise to the downside.
Goldman's O'Connor: HY AI paper widened to 389bp versus 263bp for non-AI BB/B, about 126bp extra for AI use of proceeds.

In the triple-C-or-lower bucket, 5.31% fell 5+ points last week (median week 1.2%), the fourth straight week above 5%. The 6-week count of 5+ point decliners is 147, second only to May-June 2025. Software is 32% of distressed volume against a 12% index weight. Fitch's private-debt default rate hit a record 6.3%.

Goldman's desk net sold $4.2B of tech on Friday, the most since the episode began, and $21B of TMT at the peak of the unwind (vs $23B in the July AI selloff). Global TMT L/S managers lost 11.9% in October.

Fundamental L/S lost 3.5% and systematic L/S lost 3.6% in October. Gross exposure remains elevated at 314% (97th percentile over 5 years) while net is in the 10th percentile over 1 year, so there is fuel for more volatility.
Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator had its largest drop since November 2021 but is not yet at levels that historically signal a contrarian buy.

S&P monthly returns since July were -0.13%, +2.62%, -0.45%, -0.93% against Goldman's momentum basket at -30.19%, -13.67%, +26.96%, -18.60%. NDX had its worst month versus equal-weight S&P since 2002, while S&P ex-AI had its best month (+7.64%) since ChatGPT launched. SPX 12-month implied correlation is around 20%, one of the lowest on record.

Texas holds 26.7% of planned US data center capacity. Democratic candidate Hinojosa would impose a moratorium on new data centers until regulations are in place. Markets put the stricter-regulation side at 35%. GS expects incumbent Abbott to ease regulation after the election and thinks nationwide crackdown fears are overdone.
Prediction markets give Democrats over 90% odds of taking the House and over 65% in the Senate.

Oil: crude fell below $100 on US/Iran talk headlines Monday, then rose on a Reuters report that the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island. Privorotsky is nervous the market got ahead of itself and sees a risk of re-escalation after the midterms.

Cloud revenue growth at Amazon, Google and Microsoft hit 54% y/y in Q3 (Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%). S&P EPS growth is tracking +33%. Privorotsky notes the S&P was higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950 and expects a painful year-end rally that is under-owned and hard to chase.

Privorotsky's hurdles for risk: avoid an extreme midterm outcome (Texas), then Middle East progress versus re-escalation, then whether lower oil delivers sustained rate relief. AMD and Arista report after the close and the reaction to guidance may matter as much as the guidance.

ZeroHedge's own view: a midterm relief rally is likely given washed-out positioning and friendly seasonals, but it will not fix negative FCF, the AI premium in junk, or $3.6 trillion of off-balance-sheet obligations. It compares the financing picture to 1999.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman research says the funding gap may be smaller than feared, with GS Credit estimating about $500B of hyperscaler bond capacity. Cloud revenue growth hit 54% y/y in Q3 and S&P EPS growth is tracking +33%.
tension_points.bear_case: Aggregate FCF turned negative in Q3, capex is expected at $1.2T in 2027, HY AI paper trades about 126bp wider than non-AI, and Privorotsky says debt market limits are real and binding. ZeroHedge cites $3.6T of off-balance-sheet obligations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stability in the AI trade as the market gets comfortable with corporate capital structures and the durability of revenue supporting the spend (Privorotsky's stated hurdle), and a stable reaction to AMD and Arista guidance.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects incumbent Abbott to ease regulation after the election, and Goldman research thinks nationwide crackdown fears are overdone.
tension_points.bear_case: Hinojosa would impose a moratorium on new data centers, markets put the stricter-regulation side at 35%, and Texas holds 26.7% of planned US capacity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An extreme midterm outcome, specifically the stricter-regulation side winning in Texas.

tension_points.bull_case: The S&P was higher in the 12 months following all 19 midterms since 1950, and Privorotsky expects a painful year-end rally that is under-owned and impossible to chase.
tension_points.bear_case: Momentum is unwinding, gross leverage is at the 97th percentile, and the Risk Appetite Indicator is not at contrarian-buy levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An extreme midterm outcome, Middle East re-escalation, or lower oil failing to deliver sustained relief in rates.
